q: Because the Comptroller and Auditor General assists the Public Accounts Committee at every stage of its examination of the accounts, he is popularly described, in relation to the Committee, as its:

options.A: Chairman and convenor
options.C: Friend, philosopher and guide
options.D: Executive agent

e: The Comptroller and Auditor General assists the Public Accounts Committee at every stage with audit reports and evidence, and is therefore called its friend, philosopher and guide.

q: The detailed scrutiny of the Demands for Grants of the Ministries by Departmentally Related Standing Committees, before the Demands are voted, is a system that began when these Committees were set up in the year:
e: Detailed scrutiny of Demands for Grants by Departmentally Related Standing Committees before voting began with setting up of these Committees in 1993.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament, which examines the reports and accounts of public undertakings including the railway public sector undertakings, was first constituted in the year:
e: The Committee on Public Undertakings, examining reports and accounts of public undertakings, was first constituted in 1964 on the Krishna Menon Committee recommendation.

q: In the normal course, the Supplementary Demands for Grants that arise during a financial year are bunched together and presented to Parliament in:

options.A: One batch only
options.C: Five batches
options.D: Three batches

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants arising during a year are normally bunched and presented to Parliament in three batches during the year.

q: A Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Railways is put to the vote of the Lok Sabha and passed. After it has been so passed (voted), the Demand becomes:

options.A: An Appropriation
options.C: A Grant
options.D: A Budget Allotment

e: A Demand for Grant voted and passed by the Lok Sabha becomes a Grant; it becomes an appropriation only after the Appropriation Act is passed under Article 114.

q: The Coaching Earnings of the Railways, as classified in the railway accounts, comprise:

options.A: Passenger Earnings and Other Coaching Earnings
options.C: Goods Earnings and Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Passenger Earnings and Sundry Other Earnings

e: Coaching Earnings in railway classification comprise Passenger Earnings and Other Coaching Earnings, distinct from Goods Earnings and Sundry Other Earnings.

q: Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways are kept out of the apportionment of earnings among the zonal railways because:

options.A: They are too small in amount to be apportioned
options.B: They accrue wholly to the railway on which they arise, being in the nature of local and miscellaneous receipts which do not arise from the carriage of traffic over more than one railway
options.C: They are accounted for centrally by the Railway Board
options.D: They form part of the Public Account of India

e: Sundry Other Earnings are not apportioned because they accrue wholly to the railway on which they arise as local and miscellaneous receipts not arising from carriage over more than one railway.

q: The apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the zonal railways, worked out in the Traffic Book compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office, is carried out:

options.A: Once a year, at the time of closing of the annual accounts
options.B: Only at the time of preparation of the Budget Estimates
options.C: Half-yearly, through the Debt Head Report
options.D: Every month, through the Traffic Book

e: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings among zonal railways is carried out every month through the Traffic Book compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: A clerk in the Traffic Accounts Office proposes to also apportion the Sundry Other Earnings of the railway among all the zonal railways. Apportionment is actually carried out only in respect of:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings only
options.B: All earnings, including Sundry Other Earnings
options.C: Coaching earnings and Goods earnings
options.D: Passenger earnings only

e: Apportionment is carried out only for Coaching earnings and Goods earnings from through traffic; Sundry Other Earnings are retained wholly by the earning railway.

q:
Consider the following statements about the head 'Transfer Railways' in the books of the Railway Board:
1. Balances under the head remain outstanding because cash is physically transferred from one railway to another.
2. Balances under the head represent inter-railway transfer transactions awaiting final adjustment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Balances under Transfer Railways represent inter-railway transfer transactions awaiting final adjustment in Board books, not physical cash transfers, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Two advances made by a zonal railway are under discussion in the Accounts Office. Consider the following statements about such advances:
1. An advance of the 'Miscellaneous Advances (Capital)' type is booked as revenue expenditure under Major Head 3002.
2. An advance of the 'Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue)' type is held under a suspense head until it is recovered or adjusted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are not booked as revenue expenditure under Major Head 3002, while Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are held under a suspense head till recovered or adjusted, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: A railway servant covered under the National Pension System retires. His accumulations under the System are:

options.A: Held in the Railway Pension Fund
options.B: Held in the State Railway Provident Fund
options.C: Retained permanently in the Public Account of India
options.D: Transferred to the NPS Trust and invested through the pension fund managers

e: Accumulations of an NPS subscriber are held with the NPS Trust and invested through pension fund managers, not in Railway Pension Fund or State Railway Provident Fund.

q: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG) is paid to a retired railway servant covered under the old pension scheme. The payment is debited to:

options.A: The working expenses under Major Head 3002
options.C: The Railway Pension Fund
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity for old pension scheme railway servants is a pensionary benefit debited to the Railway Pension Fund.

q: On retirement, a railway servant covered under the old pension scheme claims the cash equivalent of the leave salary standing to his credit. A clerk proposes to debit this leave encashment payment to the State Railway Provident Fund. The payment is correctly debited to:

options.A: The Railway Pension Fund
options.C: The Capital Fund
options.D: The Development Fund

e: Leave encashment on retirement for old pension scheme servants is a pensionary charge debited to the Railway Pension Fund, not to State Railway Provident Fund.

q: Certain railway lines are maintained by the Railways for strategic (defence) considerations and run at a working loss. The working losses of such Strategic Lines are:

options.A: Borne by the Development Fund
options.B: Borne by General Revenues, which reimburse the Railways on strategic considerations
options.C: Borne by the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Written off against the Capital Fund

e: Working losses of Strategic Lines maintained for defence are borne by General Revenues, which reimburse the Railways on strategic considerations.

q: The market borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation are serviced by the Railways through lease charges. In relation to the Government of India, these borrowings:

options.A: Form part of the internal debt of the Government of India
options.B: Are serviced directly out of the Consolidated Fund of India as charged expenditure
options.C: Are guaranteed to be repaid out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Do not form part of the internal debt of the Government of India

e: IRFC market borrowings are borrowings of the Railways serviced through lease charges and do not form part of internal debt of the Government of India.

q:
Consider the following statements about the cash balances of the Railways:
1. The cash balances of the Railways form part of the overall cash balance of the Government of India with the Reserve Bank of India.
2. Each zonal railway maintains a separate ways and means account with the Reserve Bank of India, distinct from the cash balance of the Government of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: 2 only

e: Railway cash balances form part of the overall cash balance of Government of India with RBI; zonal railways have no separate ways and means account, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'Excess Grant' from a 'Supplementary Grant'?

options.A: An Excess Grant is obtained after the close of the financial year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the sanctioned grant
options.B: An Excess Grant is obtained before the expenditure is incurred
options.C: An Excess Grant is voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.D: An Excess Grant is not required to be covered by an Appropriation Act

e: An Excess Grant under Article 115 is obtained after close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the sanctioned grant, unlike a Supplementary Grant obtained in advance.

q: Expenditure on a new service can be met from savings available within the grant by re-appropriation, but the approval of Parliament is nevertheless required for the new service. That approval is obtained by presenting:

options.A: An Excess Grant
options.C: An Exceptional Grant
options.D: A token supplementary demand for a nominal amount

e: For a new service met by re-appropriation from savings within the grant, Parliament approval for the new service is obtained through a token supplementary demand for a nominal amount.

q: Expenditure is incurred on a work without obtaining the sanction of the authority competent to sanction that expenditure. In the financial rules, such expenditure is termed:

options.A: Charged expenditure
options.C: Supplementary expenditure
options.D: Unsanctioned expenditure

e: Expenditure incurred without sanction of the competent authority is termed unsanctioned expenditure in financial rules and requires regularisation by competent sanction.

q: In the railway accounting system, the subsidiary books, in which transactions are first recorded in detail before compilation into the General Books, are also described as the books of:

options.A: Final entry
options.C: Adjustment
options.D: Compilation

e: Subsidiary books where transactions are first recorded in detail before compilation into General Books are books of original entry, also called prime entry.

q: The debit balance standing under Stores Suspense, representing the value of stores held in stock in the depots, forms part of:

options.A: The Block Account of the Railways
options.B: The working expenses of the year
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The Traffic Suspense account

e: Debit balance under Stores Suspense representing stores in stock is a capital asset and forms part of the Block Account of the Railways.

q: A clerk preparing a note on Union expenditure proposes to show the grants-in-aid made by law to the States under Article 275 of the Constitution as voted expenditure. The correct constitutional treatment of such grants-in-aid is that they are:

options.A: Voted expenditure of the Union Government
options.B: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.C: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Financed from the Contingency Fund of India

e: Grants-in-aid to States under Article 275 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 275(1), not voted expenditure.

q: The Separation Convention of 1924, which separated railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India, was given effect to through:

options.A: An Act of the British Parliament
options.C: A notification issued by the Railway Board
options.D: A resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly

e: The Separation Convention of 1924 separating railway finances from general finances was given effect through a resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly.

q: A study note on Article 280 of the Constitution mentions only the sharing of taxes between the Union and the States. Besides that subject, the Finance Commission is also required under that Article to recommend:

options.A: The measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the State
options.B: The disinvestment programme of the Central Government
options.C: The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to General Finances
options.D: The borrowing limits of the public sector undertakings

e: Under Article 280(3), besides tax sharing, the Finance Commission recommends measures to augment a State Consolidated Fund to supplement resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.

q: Three FRBM statements laid with the Budget are being matched with their contents in a training note. The statement which sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing financial year is the:

options.A: Three-year rolling targets statement for the specified fiscal indicators
options.C: Assessment of the growth prospects of the economy along with the underlying assumptions
options.D: Expenditure framework for the three years following the Budget year

e: Under FRBM Rules, the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out strategic priorities of Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing financial year.

q: A member wishes to introduce in Parliament a Bill making provision for a matter specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of Article 110(1) of the Constitution. Under Article 117(1), such a Bill:

options.A: Can be introduced in either House of Parliament without any recommendation
options.B: Can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha with the recommendation of the President
options.C: Shall not be introduced or moved except on the recommendation of the President, and shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Can be introduced only after the Demands for Grants have been voted

e: Under Article 117(1), a Bill for Article 110(1)(a) to (f) matters shall not be introduced or moved except on President recommendation and shall not be introduced in Rajya Sabha.

q: On the reconstitution of the Estimates Committee of Parliament, a question arises as to who names its Chairman. Under the rules of the Committee, its Chairman is:

options.A: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.B: Nominated by the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs
options.C: The senior-most member of the Committee, by convention
options.D: Appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee

e: Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of Lok Sabha from amongst members of the Committee, under the Rules of Procedure.

q: At the close of a month, every station of a zonal railway renders one statement to the Traffic Accounts Office accounting for all its traffic transactions and showing the balance due from the station. That monthly station statement is called the:

options.A: Station Balance Sheet
options.C: Account Current
options.D: Cash Remittance Note

e: Every station renders monthly to Traffic Accounts Office a Station Balance Sheet accounting for all traffic transactions and showing balance due from the station.

q: A Station Master suggests that, to save clerical work, the earnings collected at his station may be remitted to the Cash Office or the accredited bank once a week. The rule in force requires such station earnings to be remitted:

options.A: Once a week
options.C: Once a fortnight
options.D: At the end of the month

e: Station earnings must be remitted daily to the Cash Office or accredited bank under railway cash remittance rules, not weekly or monthly.

q: Of the assured annual outlay under the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), the amount met from the internal resources of the Railways is:

options.A: Rs 10,000 crore
options.C: Rs 5,000 crore
options.D: Rs 20,000 crore

e: Of RRSK assured annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore, Rs 5,000 crore is met from Railways internal resources, the remaining Rs 15,000 crore coming from Gross Budgetary Support.

q: While finalising the Balance Sheet of a zonal railway, an accountant is unsure where to place a debit balance outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads. Such a debit balance is correctly shown:

options.A: On the liabilities side
options.C: As a footnote, outside the Balance Sheet
options.D: On the assets side, as an amount recoverable

e: A debit balance under debt, suspense and remittance heads is an amount recoverable, so it is shown on the assets side of the railway Balance Sheet.

q: A clerk, while describing the three parts of the Government accounts, places the Public Account of India in Part I along with the Consolidated Fund. The Public Account actually forms:

options.A: Part III of the Government accounts
options.B: Part I of the Government accounts
options.C: Part II of the Government accounts
options.D: A section of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Government accounts are in three parts: Part I Consolidated Fund, Part II Contingency Fund and Part III Public Account, so Public Account is Part III.

q: The balance under Manufacturing Suspense, representing the cost of jobs in progress in workshops, is exhibited in the Balance Sheet of the Railways as part of:

options.A: The Railway Pension Fund
options.B: The Block Account, on the assets side
options.C: The working expenses of the year
options.D: The Traffic Suspense account

e: Manufacturing Suspense balance for jobs in progress is a capital asset exhibited in the Balance Sheet as part of the Block Account on the assets side.

q: An annexure attached to the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways shows the adjustments made for differences in the value and quantity of stores during the year. That annexure is the:

options.A: Trial Balance
options.C: Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Suspense Register

e: The Stock Adjustment Account annexed to Appropriation Accounts shows adjustments for differences in value and quantity of stores found during stock verification in the year.

q: A station passenger-amenity work is to be financed from the Development Fund, and the Accounts Office has to indicate the correct subdivision of that Fund in the allocation. Passenger and other railway user amenity works are financed from:

options.A: DF-II
options.C: The Capital Fund
options.D: DF-I

e: Passenger and other railway user amenity works are financed from DF-I, the subdivision of Development Fund earmarked for passenger amenities.

q: An operational improvement work on a zonal railway is admittedly unremunerative, and a clerk proposes to charge it to Capital in all cases. Such unremunerative operational improvement works are actually financed from:

options.A: DF-III of the Development Fund
options.C: Capital in all cases
options.D: DF-II of the Development Fund

e: Unremunerative operational improvement works are financed from DF-III of the Development Fund, not charged to Capital in all cases.

q: Under E-Recon, a few inter-railway transfer transactions sent by a zonal railway have neither been matched nor accepted by the respondent railway even after several weeks. Until they are matched and accepted, these transactions:

options.A: Are written off automatically at the close of the month
options.B: Remain outstanding under the head 'Transfer Railways' and are pursued with the respondent railway
options.C: Are converted into cash transactions with the Reserve Bank
options.D: Are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund

e: Inter-railway transfers unmatched or unaccepted under E-Recon remain outstanding under Transfer Railways and are pursued with the respondent railway till accepted.

q: Within a grant, savings under one sanctioned work are proposed to be diverted to another work, and both works fall under the same Plan Head. At the zonal level, such a re-appropriation can be sanctioned by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.C: The General Manager of the zonal railway, with the concurrence of the associated finance
options.D: The Principal Financial Adviser alone

e: Re-appropriation between works under the same Plan Head at zonal level can be sanctioned by the General Manager with concurrence of associated finance.

q: A zonal railway proposes to move funds from one Sub-Major Head of Major Head 3002 to another Sub-Major Head of the same Major Head. Since the Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation for revenue expenditure, this re-appropriation requires the sanction of:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway
options.D: The Railway Board

e: Since Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation for revenue expenditure, re-appropriation from one Sub-Major Head of Major Head 3002 to another requires Railway Board sanction.

q: A note on financial control at the Government of India level has to name the authority which keeps watch over the Government's cash position with the Reserve Bank of India while operating exchequer control. That authority is:

options.A: The Ministry of Finance
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Estimates Committee of Parliament

e: At Government of India level, the Ministry of Finance keeps watch over Government cash position with RBI while operating exchequer control through expenditure plans.

q: Station earnings in cash reach the Cash Office of a zonal railway along with their covering documents. Before accepting the remittances, the Cash Office checks them with reference to:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets rendered to the Traffic Accounts Office
options.B: The Cash Remittance Notes accompanying the remittances
options.C: The Transfer Certificates received from other railways
options.D: The Pink Book of the railway

e: Cash Office checks station remittances with reference to Cash Remittance Notes accompanying them, which detail earnings remitted by each station.

q: In the earlier practice, a zonal railway first sent the Railway Board an advance account of the month so that the Board was not kept waiting for the final compilation. The purpose of that advance account, the Approximate Account Current, was to:

options.A: Replace the final monthly account altogether
options.B: Report only the balances under the suspense heads
options.C: Furnish the Railway Board with approximate figures of the month's transactions in advance, pending the final compilation of the account
options.D: Obtain the supplementary grant for the month

e: The Approximate Account Current furnished the Railway Board with approximate figures of the month transactions in advance, pending final compilation of the monthly account.

q: Scrap and other materials are released from a renewal work charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and their value has to be brought to account. The correct treatment of the value of such released materials is to:

options.A: Credit their value to Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Ignore them in the accounts of the work
options.C: Debit their value to Capital as a fresh asset
options.D: Credit their value to the renewal work concerned, thereby reducing the charge to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Value of scrap and released materials from a DRF renewal work is credited to that renewal work, reducing the charge to Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q: A finance note has to state how the corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF), set up in 2001-02, was built up. That corpus was made up of:

options.A: A contribution from the General Revenues (Ministry of Finance) together with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.B: The safety surcharge on passenger fares alone
options.C: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation alone
options.D: Appropriations made from the Railway Pension Fund

e: SRSF corpus was built from a contribution from General Revenues together with safety surcharge levied on passenger fares, totalling Rs 17,000 crore.

q: The first batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants in a financial year is presented in the Monsoon Session. The second batch of such Demands is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Budget Session
options.C: Monsoon Session
options.D: A special session convened for the purpose

e: Supplementary Demands are presented in three batches; the first in Monsoon Session and the second batch is ordinarily presented in the Winter Session.

q: A zonal railway shifts the payment of its bills to a centralised electronic system operated through the accredited bank, so that payments are no longer made bill by bill from each cash office. This centralised electronic payment arrangement is known as:

options.A: Computerised reservation of passenger accommodation
options.C: CIPS
options.D: Electronic auction of stores purchases

e: CIPS is the centralised electronic payment system through the accredited bank by which railway payments are made centrally instead of bill by bill from each cash office.

q: A debit is raised against a zonal railway by another railway through a Transfer Certificate, but the respondent railway finds the debit incorrect. In such a case, the respondent railway should:

options.A: Pay the amount immediately and claim a refund later
options.B: Write off the amount with the sanction of its General Manager
options.C: Charge the amount to its ordinary working expenses
options.D: Return the Transfer Certificate with its objections, the item remaining outstanding till the matter is settled

e: If a Transfer Certificate debit is incorrect, the respondent railway returns it with objections and the item remains outstanding under Transfer Railways till settled.

q: Amounts remitted by stations and offices into the bank are debited in the railway books to 'Remittances into Banks' and stay there until the bank gives credit for them. The balance under this remittance head therefore normally shows:

options.A: A debit balance, representing the remittances made into the bank which are awaiting credit by the bank
options.C: A nil balance at the close of every day
options.D: A balance only in the March accounts

e: Remittances into Banks normally show a debit balance, representing remittances made into the bank which are awaiting credit by the bank.

q: In railway accounts correspondence, the collective expression 'Debt Heads' is commonly used as a short name covering together:

options.A: The revenue heads of account only
options.B: The debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads of account
options.C: The capital heads of account only
options.D: The earnings heads of account

e: Debt Heads is the collective short name in railway accounts for debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads of account together.
